item.title: Legal & Data Protection Officer
item.description: Legal & Data Protection Officer Eurofound - The European Foundation for the Improvement of Living & Working Conditions Dublin, Ireland JOB CONTEXT & DUTIES The Organisational Support Unit provides a range of services for the efficient development and implementation of Eurofound’s operations through various planning and management information systems, workflows and management and performance reporting tools. The Unit is also responsible for supporting the Executive Director and staff in areas of legal advice, data protection, document management and internal control. The duties will require to work on a variety of organisation-wide tasks in good collaboration with colleagues in the Unit as well as with colleagues across the organisation. The Legal & Data Protection Officer will be based in the Organisational Support Unit and will contribute to the achievement of Eurofound’s objectives by providing legal advice and support on the interpretation and application of the legal framework governing Eurofound’s operational and administrative activities. The successful candidate will also be appointed as the Data Protection Officer overseeing Eurofound’s data protection strategy and implementation in accordance with the applicable Regulation (EU) 2018/1725. The duties of the post include: Legal advice and consultation: Providing input in respect of all legal aspects relevant to the functioning of Eurofound, including on matters related to staff and financial regulations, governance structure, data protection, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and contractual matters including intellectual property rights. Drafting legal opinions and documents on the application and interpretation of Eurofound’s legal framework as well as any other applicable legal provisions of Union law. Drafting decisions of the Management Board or other bodies of Eurofound’s governance structure. Contributing to the preparation and implementation of arrangements with other Union institutions and bodies, and other external partners. Cooperating with external legal advisors; including those that may represent the Agency in litigation before the Court of Justice of the European Union. Data Protection: Informing and advising staff on their obligations pursuant to the Data Protection Regulation. Preparing and monitoring policies and guidelines on data protection. Conducting regular assessments. Maintaining records of all data processing activities Serving as the point of contact between the Agency and the European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS). General: Collaborating with staff in achieving compliance with the legal framework and awareness of data protection requirements in the agency’s operations. Providing training and coaching in regulatory compliance – in collaboration with staff in HR, Internal control and ICT (on AI and cybersecurity). Representing Eurofound in inter-agency networks on legal matters and data protection. Other tasks assigned by the Head of Unit. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED The selection procedure is open to candidates who, by the closing date for applications, fulfil the following conditions: ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA Citizenship of one of the Member States of the European Union, entitled to full rights as a citizen; Have fulfilled any obligations imposed by the laws concerning military service; Have a thorough knowledge of one official language of the European Union and a satisfactory knowledge (level B2) of another language of the Union. As English is the daily working language of Eurofound, a high level of proficiency in English (C1) is required to a level necessary for the performance of the duties. at least a level of education which corresponds to completed university studies of at least three years attested by a diploma. SELECTION CRITERIA Candidates will be shortlisted on the basis of the following criteria: • University degree in law and/or advanced studies in law with a focus on some or all of: Administrative law, EU law and data protection; • At least three years’ experience in areas of relevance to this role in legal practice or advice and data protection; • Experience of administrative and routine work and evidence of a clear understanding of the duties that the role of Legal and Data Protection Officer entails, preferably within the framework of EU institutions and bodies. In addition to the above, candidates who are invited for testing and interview will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria: Excellent writing skills; Excellent verbal communication skills with the ability to explain the practical implications of rules and regulations through different formats supporting organisational learning and compliance; Excellent digital skills; Excellent analytical skills; Ability to manage own workload and adapt as necessary to changing demands and hard deadlines. Collaborative team player, capable of working autonomously when necessary; Ability to work effectively in an international or multicultural environment; Proof of meeting eligibility criteria - by means of appropriate documents (copies of educational certificates, references from employers, etc.) - must be provided if requested. Apply Now Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying.

Legal and technical work: prepare legal and technical analysis; produce questionnaires and information material; contribute to policy and operational documentation; monitor jurisprudence of the Court of Justice of the European Union. Member and stakeholder liaison: liaise with Member Bureaux, Guarantee Funds, Compensation Bodies and Information Centres; maintain constructive contact with external partners (including United Nations Economic Commission for Europe and the European Commission). International coordination: support exchanges with the insurance sector and European Institutions; travel mainly in Europe from time to time when required. The offer Full-time open-ended contract; Pleasant and international working environment at COB Secretariat; Competitive salary package with extra-legal benefits, including group insurance, hospitalisation insurance, mobility budget, luncheon vouchers and 13 th month; Flexible organisation of work (including telework) where the agenda allows; Training and education opportunities in line with the position; Office on Avenue Louise, easily accessible by public transport. Send to: Alexandra Sibille, Administrative Manager & HR Coordinator, at hr@cobx.org . Deadline: 30 September 2026 Only selected candidates will be contacted for further steps of the recruitment and selection procedure. COB is committed to conducting the recruitment and selection procedure in a professional, respectful and confidential manner. Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying.

item.description: Policy Assistant for European Institutions (CIP Internship) (Six Months) EEB - European Environmental Bureau Brussels, Belgium € 1 300 per month net Come join Europe’s largest network of environmental citizens’ organisations and contribute as a policy assistant with a Convention d’Immersion Professionelle (CIP) to its work on the next EU budget (multi annual financial framework - MFF) for a better future where people and nature thrive together. About us The EEB is the largest network of environmental citizens’ organisations in Europe. We bring together over 190 member organisations from more than 40 countries, representing some 30 million individual members and supporters. We advocate for progressive policies to create a better future where people and nature thrive together. About the internship The EEB offers paid internships under a Convention d’Immersion Professionelle (CIP), which is a scheme for organisations based in the Brussels Region under the supervision of Bruxelles Formation. A CIP internship is therefore a paid internship with a trilateral contract between the intern, the EEB and Bruxelles Formation and is regulated under Belgian law. A CIP contract does not constitute an employment relationship, and an intern is therefore not an employee of the organisation. CIP internships are only available to graduates, that is, individuals who are not students anymore. CIP contracts cannot be offered to enrolled students. Interns who are neither Belgian citizens nor graduates from Belgian universities are, according to the legal framework, eligible for CIP contracts for up to 12 months (as opposed to 6 months for Belgians and Belgian graduates). Our commitment to fairness, equality, diversity and wellbeing The EEB strives to be a fair, inclusive, safe place and a welcoming and learning organisation. We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage applications from a diverse range of candidates. Your experience matters. Please consult our Diversity, Equality and Inclusion Policy . Please do not use pictures in your CV. Do leave out any information that may contribute to unconscious bias such as reference to your nationality, date or place of birth. We respect our employees’ lives outside of work, support colleagues in care roles, and take work-life balance and wellbeing seriously. How You Will Have an Impact As our policy assistant for European Institutions, you will join a strategic horizontal and cross cutting team of the organisation managed directly by the EEB Policy Director and supported by the European Institutions policy officer that covers essential horizontal policies. You will in particular be given the chance to contribute to and influence a set of key legislations that are instrumental to the future of EU environmental and climate actions while monitoring other key horizontal developments impacting EU environmental laws such as simplification and key milestones (EU presidencies etc.). Your role will also provide you with the opportunity to closely engage with EEB national members and other partners such as other EU large environmental networks. What You Will Actually Do Support the coordination efforts of EEB MFF advocacy (in particular help with the monitoring of relevant legislative developments, meetings with EEB members or colleagues, ensure good internal communication flows on the topic); Support mobilisation and advocacy efforts of the broader environmental coalition working on MFF (take part in the weekly meetings of the coalition and help prepare them, support collective actions when needed (calls with members, gatherings, advocacy meetings)); Support the EEB European Institutions and Governance team horizontal policy work (in particular help with the weekly newsletter, help with the different horizontal policy task forces (minutes, follow up)). Who You Are As EEB’s future policy assistant for European Institutions (CIP internship) , you will have a Bachelor/master's degree OR relevant experience, a basic understanding of European legislation related to the Multi Annual Financial Framework and a strong interest in working for an environmental organisation. Your Skills & Experiences Bachelor/Masters degree OR relevant experience; A basic understanding of European legislation related to the Multi annual Financial Framework; Good written and spoken English; Ability to work both autonomously and in a team; Ability to communicate in a multicultural environment; Capability to prioritize and work with several projects at the same time; Ability to take own initiatives in different situations; Familiarity with cloud document collaboration; Prepared and able to work in a dynamic working environment; Interest in working in an environmental organisation. Assets That Make You Stand Out Working knowledge of French and any other language skills is an asset. Your Values You care about the environment and subscribe to the EEB’s values. Why You Will Love Working With Us A 6-months full-time contract under the Bruxelles Formation “convention d’immersion professionnelle” – paid internship of 1 300EUR net/month coupled with various benefits: transport costs reimbursement, luncheon vouchers, working from home indemnity; An attractive workspace in the heart of the EU quarter and a healthy organisational culture , including, for instance, staff away days and (optional) social gatherings; Possibility to work from home 4 days a week ; Flexible working hours with a transparent floating time system . How You Can Apply Please send your CV, a cover letter explaining your motivation and a reply to the question below to apply for this position to personnel@eeb.org . Please save the application as a pdf and the subject of your email must clearly state: “Policy Assistant for European Institutions”. Question for the post of Policy Assistant for European Institutions One of the priorities of the EEB is to secure adequate funding for nature and environmental protection in the next EU budget. If you had six months to support this work, what would success look like for you? Important: To determine your eligibility, in your email, please confirm that you have not been employed on a ‘convention d’immersion professionnelle’ (CIP) contract in the past and that you are not currently enrolled in a university. item.description: Vertaler en Conferentietolk (m/v) Moedertaal Nederlands Eureca Strasbourg, France KLAAR VOOR EEN NIEUWE UITDAGING? De Centrale Commissie voor de Rijnvaart (CCR) heeft sinds 1815 als belangrijkste taak het waarborgen van de veiligheid en de welvaart van de Rijnvaart . Deze internationale organisatie staat bekend om haar belangrijke rol in de binnenvaart en is actief op het snijvlak van technische, sociale en milieuvraagstukken. Het wervingsbureau Eureca zoekt voor deze organisatie een vertaler en conferentietolk (m/v) met Nederlands als moedertaal , ter versterking van het team van vertalers. Functie op basis van een tijdelijk contract (duur: 4 jaar) met zicht op omzetting naar een vast contract. Mooi kantoor in het hart van Straatsburg met de mogelijkheid tot gedeeltelijk thuiswerken . DE FUNCTIE DIE WIJ JE AANBIEDEN Je rapporteert aan de secretaris-generaal en maakt deel uit van het team van vertalers. Jouw taken omvatten: Het vertalen van redactionele, technische en soms politiek gevoelige teksten vanuit het Duits en het Frans naar het Nederlands , met inachtneming van deadlines, kwaliteitseisen en de geldende terminologie, waarbij je je werklast zelfstandig en flexibel indeelt; Het volgen van ontwikkelingen binnen de werkterreinen van de organisatie en van terminologische en taalkundige ontwikkelingen, en het actualiseren van vertaalgeheugens en woordenlijsten; Nauwe samenwerking met de auteurs over taalkundige en stilistische keuzes; Simultaan vertalen van het Duits naar het Nederlands en omgekeerd tijdens vergaderingen, werkgroepen en gesprekken met tolk die plaatsvinden op het hoofdkantoor van de organisatie; Voorbereiding van elke tolkopdracht: bestudering van de werkdocumenten, de agenda en videomateriaal, gericht terminologisch onderzoek. WAT DEZE FUNCTIE AANTREKKELIJK MAAKT Het opbouwen van specialistische expertise op technisch, politiek en sectoraal gebied; Goede begeleiding tijdens je inwerkperiode; Werken in een internationale, dynamische en stimulerende werkomgeving. JE BENT GESCHIKT VOOR DEZE FUNCTIE ALS Je bent afgestudeerd met een master in vertalen en conferentietolken en beheerst naast je moedertaal, het Nederlands, ook het Duits uitstekend. Een goede beheersing van het Frans (B2 – C1) is een pluspunt voor vertalingen naar het Nederlands; Je hebt minimaal 3 jaar ervaring in vertalen en tolken; Je bent georganiseerd, nauwgezet en werkt graag in teamverband. Maar bovenal heb je passie voor kwaliteit! UW VOORDELEN Een contract voor een periode van 4 jaar met de mogelijkheid tot omzetting in een contract voor onbepaalde tijd na afloop van deze 4 jaar; Een belastingvrij nettosalaris; Een goede ziektekosten- en pensioenverzekering; Een werkweek van 38 uur, met de mogelijkheid om 2 dagen per week thuis te werken, en 30 vakantiedagen per jaar. Solliciteer door je cv en motivatiebrief te sturen naar: cbouquet@eureca-rh.com . Traducteur H/F Natif Néerlandais Eureca Strasbourg, France PRÊT(E) POUR UN NOUVEAU DÉFI ? La Commission centrale pour la navigation du Rhin (CCNR) est une organisation internationale de plus de 200 ans dont le siège est à Strasbourg. Elle compte cinq États membres (Allemagne, Belgique, France, Pays-Bas et Suisse) et a pour mission principale d’assurer la sécurité et la prospérité de la navigation rhénane. La CCNR est une organisation à la pointe de l’innovation pour permettre à la flotte rhénane d’être à l’avant-garde et de faire face aux défis d’aujourd’hui: la digitalisation, le verdissement, l’automatisation, l’adaptation au changement climatique, les qualifications du personnel ou encore la position économique du secteur. Au-delà du Rhin, de nombreuses activités de la CCNR sont maintenant réalisées dans un cadre européen. Le cabinet de recrutement Eureca recherche pour cette organisation un Traducteur H/F, de langue maternelle néerlandaise , pour renforcer son équipe linguistique. Poste en CDD (durée de 4 ans) et perspective de transformation en CDI. De beaux locaux en plein cœur de Strasbourg avec possibilité de télétravail partiel . LA MISSION QUE L’ON VOUS PROPOSE Rattaché(e) à la secrétaire générale et au sein de l’équipe de traducteurs, vos missions incluent: (80% du temps) Traduction de l’allemand et du français vers le néerlandais de textes rédactionnels, techniques et parfois politiquement sensibles, dans le respect des délais, des exigences de qualité et de la terminologie en vigueur en organisant votre charge de travail avec autonomie et flexibilité; Veille sur les domaines d'activité de l’organisation ainsi que sur les nouveautés terminologiques et linguistiques et mise à jour des mémoires de traduction et glossaires; Collaboration étroite avec les auteurs sur les choix linguistiques et stylistiques; (20% du temps) Ponctuellement, interprétation simultanée de l’allemand vers le néerlandais et inversement à l’occasion de réunions, groupes de travail et entretiens interprétés se tenant au siège de l’organisation; Préparation de chaque mission d’interprétation: prise de connaissance des documents de travail, de l’ordre du jour, des support vidéo, recherche terminologique ciblée. VOUS AIMEREZ Développer une véritable expertise sectorielle, technique ou politique, au fil des textes; Bénéficier d'un accompagnement lors de votre intégration pour faciliter votre prise de poste; Evoluer dans un environnement de travail international, dynamique et stimulant. VOUS RÉUSSIREZ À CE POSTE SI Diplômé(e) d’un Master en traduction , vous avez une excellente maîtrise de l’allemand en plus de votre langue maternelle, le néerlandais. Une bonne maîtrise du français (B2 – C1) est un atout; Idéalement, vous êtes diplômé(e) d’un Master en interprétation avec l’allemand et le néerlandais comme langues de travail ; Vous bénéficiez d’une expérience de 3 ans minimum en traduction et idéalement en interprétation; Organisé(e), vous êtes rigoureux(se) et vous appréciez le travail en équipe. Mais avant tout, vous avez la passion du travail bien fait! VOS AVANTAGES Un contrat de 4 ans avec une possibilité de conversion en CDI à l’issue de ces 4 années; Une rémunération nette d’impôts; Une bonne couverture santé et prévoyance; Une semaine de travail de 38 heures, 2 jours de télétravail par semaine, 30 jours de congés par an. item.description: Civil Society Fund Transnational Officer Position - VA 29/2026 FMO - Financial Mechanism Office Brussels, Belgium From € 117,072 per year Are you a dynamic and highly motivated professional looking to make a positive impact in Europe? Join our team in the Civil Society Fund at the Financial Mechanism Office (FMO) in Brussels to work on strengthening a vibrant and resilient civil society protecting democracy, the rule of law and human rights. You will be responsible for the new component called “Civil Society Fund -Transnational (CSF-TN)” working at European level. The position is open to nationals of the EEA EFTA States (Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway) and to the nationals of the Beneficiary States of EEA and Norway Grants (Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia). About us: The Financial Mechanism Office (FMO) - affiliated with the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) - is the international secretariat carrying out the day-to-day management of the EEA and Norway Grants. The Grants are Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway’s contribution to reducing economic and social disparities in the European Economic Area (EEA) and strengthen bilateral relations and partnerships between the Donor States and the 15 Beneficiary States (Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia). The EEA Grants are financed by the three donor countries whereas Norway Grants are financed solely by Norway. The current funding period has a total budget of 3.2 billion euros. The programmes in this funding period will focus on these overall priorities: European green transition; Democracy, rule of law and human rights; Social inclusion and resilience. Why join the FMO? We offer more than just a job. We offer a stimulating and diverse international workplace with a trust-based culture. Our team of more than 60 employees from the EEA region brings a rich blend of experiences and knowledge to our daily operations. We are committed to fostering a collaborative and respectful environment where you can advance your career. Every day, our work is driven by a shared goal: a green, democratic and resilient Europe where everyone can take a meaningful part in shaping their lives. We work closely with the Ministries of Foreign Affairs of the Donor States (Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway), the 15 Beneficiary States and various international partners. Learn more: If you are ready to take on a rewarding challenge and be part of a dedicated team working towards improving economic and social equality and strengthening cooperation and partnerships in Europe, we encourage you to apply. For more details about our work and the opportunities we offer, please visit our website at www.eeagrants.org . Scope: You will be part of the Civil Society Team within the Funds and Horizontal Concerns Unit, reporting to the Unit’s Head. The Civil Society Fund Transnational (CSF-TN) is a newly established instrument which aims at strengthening capacity, cooperation, and resilience of institutions and civil society to protect and promote democracy, the rule of law, and human rights at European level. The Financial Mechanism Office (FMO) acts as the Fund Operator on behalf of the Donors. The thematic focus of the CSF-TN is civic space and civil society engagement; information integrity and disinformation; and competence and knowledge development for democratic resilience. The CSF-TN Officer is responsible for the overall day-to-day management of the fund. The position combines operational fund management responsibilities with coordination of policy and programme content expertise to ensure that CSF-TN initiatives are aligned with the objectives of the EEA and Norway Grants. The position will involve external representation and engagement with relevant stakeholders; travel will be required. You may be required to work in other areas, according to the needs and priorities of the FMO. Main Responsibilities and tasks: Administration and compliance: As Fund Operator, the FMO is responsible for the technical, administrative and financial management of the CSF-TN. The CSF-TN Officer will: Manage the full grant lifecycle. Follow up grant agreements, work plans and reporting requirements, organise annual meetings and monitor implementation progress, risks, budgets and results across the portfolio; Coordinate closely with legal, finance and management colleagues to ensure sound financial management, and compliance with applicable regulations, Donor requirements and principles of accountability and transparency. Coordination of the CSF-TN portfolio: Responsibilities include: Oversee the CSF-TN portfolio, ensuring its effective implementation and alignment with EEA and Norway Grants objectives, following Donor priorities and Senior Management guidance; Facilitate synergies between the CSF-TN, initiatives implemented by the International Partners Organisations, Civil Society Funds and other relevant EEA and Norway Grants initiatives; Analyse trends, risks and opportunities on the thematic focus of the CSF-TN; Assess the relevance and added value of proposed initiatives in cooperation with relevant FMO colleagues; Support Donor engagement through briefing notes and strategic analysis; Represent the FMO in meetings with European networks, civil society organisations, think tanks, foundations and international partners. Qualifications: A Master’s degree in a relevant field. Required Experience: At least 6 years of relevant professional experience; Experience in grant management, programme or project management; Experience working with civil society organisations, international organisations, public bodies or European networks; Experience in managing complex stakeholder relationships. Desired experience: Knowledge of European civil society ecosystems and networks; Experience working on democratic governance, civic space or information integrity. Required skills: Strong project and portfolio management skills; Knowledge of grant management, compliance and financial oversight; Strong organisational skills; Strong analytical skills and drafting skills; Ability to work autonomously and proactively; Strong interpersonal skills; Presentation skills; ability to present complex matters clearly. A great work environment and strong teamwork define the FMO, and we look for candidates who actively contribute to both. Language: Excellent oral and written communication skills in English (the working language of the FMO). Fluency in any of the Donor or Beneficiary State languages would be an advantage. Employment terms: Job reference: VA 29/2026 Duration of appointment: This is a fixed-term contract for three years. The contract is renewable once, subject to the renewal being in the interest of the FMO and to a decision on the new funding period following the current Financial Mechanisms. Start date: As soon as possible Grade: A4 A nnual starting salary: EUR 117,072 Appointments are normally made at step 1 of the grade. The Managing Director of the FMO reserves the right to appoint a candidate at a level different from that advertised. The FMO is an employer dedicated to the principles of diversity and equality. We are committed to promoting and nurturing a diverse and inclusive workplace, with a healthy work-life balance. FMO offers a hybrid working model for its staff. Subject to the requirements of the role, operational needs, and in agreement with their line manager, staff may work up to 40% of their weekly working hours from a location other than the office according to the current policy. The duty station for all FMO staff is Brussels, Belgium. We offer stimulating and meaningful work in a diverse international environment, with the opportunity to collaborate with highly skilled professionals from across Europe. Salaries and related payments are exempt from taxation in the EFTA Member States, and as regulated in headquarters agreements, in the EFTA host states. Depending on the candidate’s family status, and individual circumstances, additional benefits and allowances may apply. Candidates should carefully consider their individual tax circumstances. This is particularly important where personal circumstances may give rise to tax obligations in countries other than the EFTA Member States of the EFTA host states. For questions related to the recruitment process, please contact us by email: fmorecruitment@efta.int . In case of technical issues with the recruitment tool, please contact: hr.support@efta.int . Please note that only applications received via FMO’s recruitment tool will be considered. Deadline for submission of applications: Wednesday, 28 October 2026 (midnight, Brussels time) . item.description: Campaign Director EJF - Environmental Justice Foundation Brussels, London or Berlin Contract: Three years. Hybrid working arrangements are in place Salary range: Dependent upon experience and location Applications: Please apply by 3 November 2026 About the Environmental Justice Foundation The Environmental Justice Foundation (EJF) exists to protect the natural world and uphold our fundamental human right to a secure environment. We work at the frontlines of environmental injustice, alongside communities most affected by climate breakdown, biodiversity loss, and exploitation - transforming evidence into action, and injustice into lasting change. EJF is a global non-profit driven by a powerful belief: that environmental protection and human rights are inseparable. Through courageous field investigations, rigorous research, and strategic international advocacy, we expose environmental crime, challenge impunity, and catalyse systemic reform. Our work delivers real-world impact, shaping policy, strengthening governance, protecting vital ecosystems, and defending those who risk their lives to safeguard them. Our campaigns span four deeply interconnected areas: oceans, climate, forests and wetlands, and the training, protection, and empowerment of environmental defenders and journalists. From illegal fishing and forced labour to deforestation, land grabs, and climate displacement, we confront some of the most complex and urgent crises of our time - always with a focus on accountability, equity, and durable solutions. EJF is an international organisation with a diverse team working across four continents, united by a shared ambition: to protect people by protecting the planet. We are bold, evidence-led, and impact-driven. We speak truth to power - and we build pathways to a fairer, more resilient future. Join Us. About the role Over the next three years, Europe will make critical decisions that will shape the future of its seas and the global ocean for decades. During this decisive policy cycle, multiple foundational frameworks will be introduced, some might be reviewed. This is occurring amid rising political pressure for deregulation: weakening EU environmental protections would not only harm marine ecosystems and fish populations, but it would also threaten coastal livelihoods and undermine the EU’s credibility as a global standard-setter in ocean governance. This situation highlights the urgent need to reframe the public debate and policies around sustainability and low-impact fishers to achieve economic resilience, climate stability, and social equity, which are foundational to a sustainable future for Europe and beyond. EJF is working with close partners to lead a campaign to both defend and secure a robust, fit-for-purpose EU regulatory regime that protects marine ecosystems and restores biodiversity while finally ensuring a more equitable and sustainable fishing sector and putting an end to the marginalisation of small-scale fishers. Our vision is of thriving seas and thriving coastal communities going hand in hand, where a healthy ocean is the bedrock of sustainable livelihoods, jobs, and long-term economic prosperity. It is this inseparable link that will drive our engagement. The Campaign Director will lead the implementation of this flagship campaign, combining deep institutional knowledge, strategic influence, and outstanding communication skills with the credibility and networks necessary to operate at the highest levels of European policymaking. Key responsibilities The Campaign Director will: Lead a flagship EU campaign strategy to defend and secure strong, science-based and fair ocean policies during the current European policy cycle; Co-develop and co-execute high-impact advocacy plans targeting the European Commission, European Parliament, Council of the EU, and Member State governments, ensuring timely influence at key political moments; Establish and maintain close relationships and constructive collaborations with NGOs, fishers’ organisations, academics, legal experts and other allies to maximise influence and alignment; Coordinate the delivery of work across team members across the coalition to deliver the campaign; Build and maintain senior-level political relationships with policymakers, advisers, diplomats, regulators and other decision-makers to advance campaign objectives; Lead debate framing and messaging that position healthy seas, biodiversity restoration and thriving coastal communities as mutually reinforcing priorities; Represent, as needed and appropriate, the campaign externally in high-level meetings, conferences, roundtables, media opportunities and stakeholder forums with authority and credibility; Identify political opportunities and risks, providing strategic intelligence and recommendations to adapt campaign tactics in a fast-moving policy environment; Secure measurable policy outcomes, tracking progress against campaign goals and working with the collaboration to adjust strategies to maximise impact; Ensure strong delivery, accountability and value for money; Contribute to donor engagement, including helping shape proposals, reporting on impact and supporting opportunities. Person specification Essential: You will have sharp political insight and strategic vision, be results-driven, demonstrate strong initiative, have credibility in senior policy environments, and be able to represent the campaign with authority and professionalism. You will have: Senior political expertise and access: A highly experienced professional with a deep understanding of the European institutions and established networks across officials and influential political groups; Proven campaign leadership: Demonstrable track record of designing and delivering successful, high-impact advocacy or political campaigns with measurable outcomes; Collaborative and diplomatic approach: Able to work constructively with diverse stakeholders, build coalitions, and inspire external partners and allies to support shared objectives. This should include the ability to work across governments, NGOs and industry; Outstanding communicator : A persuasive and authoritative communicator capable of engaging senior policymakers, partners, and public audiences. Must be fluent in English. Desirable: Fluent in at least one additional EU language, with French, German, or Spanish strongly preferred. Benefits Annual leave increases with length of service; Up to two days of remote working per week. The other three days will be based in EJF’s offices in Brussels, London or Berlin; A “Cycle to Work” scheme; A highly motivated and open-minded team of committed colleagues, and the opportunity to develop and deliver persuasive proposals contributing to EJF’s campaign and organisational objectives; Excellent opportunities for professional growth and personal development. How to apply To apply, please complete the application form using the Apply Now button below. This includes: A cover letter outlining your suitability for the role (max 2 pages); Your CV (max 2 pages) The deadline for applications is 6pm CET on 3 November 2026 . Interview processes and the number of rounds for different roles will vary, but are likely to include three stages: a short screening call, a panel interview with a task relevant to the role, and a final interview. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Candidates must have the legal right to work in Belgium, the United Kingdom or Germany. item.description: Behavioural Insights Researcher A 2-year Contract BEUC - The European Consumer Organisation Brussels, Belgium € 4.204 - € 4.476 per month gross BEUC-The European Consumer Organisation is seeking a Behavioural Insights Researcher to strengthen the evidence base underpinning its consumer policy, enforcement, and advocacy work. Your role: The successful candidate is expected to contribute to BEUC’s enforcement and advocacy work , especially in the areas related to the implementation of the Digital Markets Act , by bringing behavioural insights - including coordinating data analysis on consumer behaviour and market practices - to BEUC’s work to better understand how consumers’ decision-making processes affect the effectiveness of regulatory interventions. The tasks will include, inter alia: Supporting BEUC's policy and enforcement teams by providing behavioural evidence and analysis in support of advocacy, litigation, complaints, and other regulatory discussions; Analysing consumer behaviour and decision-making in areas such as digital services, e-commerce, sustainability, financial services, and consumer rights; Contributing to the design and implementation of behavioural research projects , including experiments, surveys, field studies, and consumer testing; Translating research findings into clear policy recommendations and practical insights; Managing relationships with external stakeholders (e.g., research institutes, consultants, academic partners); Presenting findings to colleagues, consumer organisations, policymakers, regulators, and other stakeholders; Monitoring developments in behavioural science relevant to consumer policy and market regulation; Contributing to publications, reports, position papers, and presentations. The selected candidate will dedicate 80% of the time to implement these tasks in relation to the Digital Markets Act and 20% to other consumer priorities. Your profile: Master's degree or PhD in behavioural economics, behavioural science, psychology, economics, data science, or a related field; Strong analytical skills and experience conducting behavioural research using quantitative and/or experimental methods; Strong interest in consumer policy , market regulation, and public-interest work; Ability to communicate complex findings clearly to non-specialist audiences; Excellent drafting skills in English (an additional language is an asset); Ability to manage projects independently and work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams. What we offer: A full-time 2-year contract with a competitive salary package: A gross monthly salary in the indicative range of €4.204 and €4.476 gross , depending on experience; Fringe benefits: Meal vouchers, group insurance, homeworking allowance, public transport, 6 days extra-legal paid leave; Flexitime , homeworking possibility (up to 3 days per week), work-life balance; 20 days/year working from abroad; External consultant contracts are also welcome. A workplace committed to support the growth, skills and well-being of its staff through extensive training and well-being activities; A multidisciplinary and multicultural working environment within an organisation dedicated to promoting consumer interests; A team of experienced consumer advocates who need you to voice efficiently their policy arguments to EU stakeholders; A non-routine job: The opportunity to deliver positive impact in an exciting international organisation with a dynamic, committed and fun team in the heart of Brussels. Location: As our contracts are subject to Belgian law, candidates must be committed to official registration in Belgium and working from our Brussels office. We offer teleworking possibilities from home or abroad, subject to our remote working policy and organisational needs. Hiring process: Applications for the position should be sent by 08 November 2026 by e-mail to apply@beuc.eu with subject line: Behavioural insights researcher .
